hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason:
BLOCKED by dcg

Tip: dcg explain "rm -rf /"

Reason: rm -rf on root or home paths is EXTREMELY DANGEROUS. This command will NOT be executed without review of the exact target and authorization.

Explanation: This command would recursively delete files starting from the root filesystem (/) or home directory (~). This is catastrophic and will destroy:
             
             - Your entire operating system
             - All installed applications and libraries
             - All user data, documents, and configurations
             - Boot files, making the system unbootable
             
             There is NO recovery without backups. Even with backups, full restoration takes hours to days.
             
             dcg auto-allows recursive deletion only for literal temp paths:
               rm -rf /tmp/<subdir>/scratch
             
             Inspect the exact intended target with ls -la /path/to/directory. Review unique work and active consumers, and establish explicit authorization for that exact action. Retain blocked state in place; do not move or copy root or home contents to another deletion path.

Rule: core.filesystem:rm-rf-root-home

Retain the affected state in place and report this exact blocked action and reason. Do not move or archive it merely to get around this denial.

When explicit user authorization covers this exact reviewed action, including authorization already given, permit only this command once with: dcg allow-once <DYNAMIC> --single-use

remediation.safeAlternative: Inspect the exact target and preserve unique work. Retain it in place while the reviewed removal remains blocked.
